hints: Look at the two -OH groups in ethylene glycol and think about what type of intermolecular force they can make with water and ice.
Remember ice is held in an open lattice by hydrogen bonds, so consider how a molecule that can also hydrogen bond would affect that lattice.
Think about the rule that like dissolves like, and decide if a small molecule with two -OH groups will mix with the water it helps to melt.
walkthrough:
**Spot the hydrogen bonding groups**

Think of ethylene glycol as a small organic molecule with two alcohol groups. Each -OH has an H attached to O for donating, and lone pairs on O for accepting.

Structure to keep in mind:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Check statement 1 - disrupting ice**

Ice is a giant network of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ molecules held by extensive hydrogen bonds in an open lattice. When ethylene glycol is added, it forms its own hydrogen bonds to water, competing with water-water bonds.

Idea:
$$\text{water-water H-bonds (ice lattice) + glycol} \rightarrow \text{water-glycol H-bonds (disrupted lattice)}$$

**Check statement 2 - glycol to glycol bonding**

Pure ethylene glycol is a liquid with relatively strong intermolecular forces. The -OH groups allow one $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ molecule to hydrogen bond to another one, just like in water and alcohols. So statement 2 is true.

**Check statement 3 - dissolving in melt water**

Small molecules with -OH groups are hydrophilic and mix very well with water. Ethylene glycol forms hydrogen bonds with water, so it dissolves readily in the water formed from melting ice. So statement 3 is true.

Conclusion: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.

options.A: Correct. All three statements are true. Glycol disrupts the H-bond network of ice (1), forms H-bonds with itself via its two -OH groups (2), and dissolves in water by H-bonding to water (3).
options.B: Incorrect. This option suggests only 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is also correct because ethylene glycol with two polar -OH groups is fully miscible with water through hydrogen bonding.
options.C: Incorrect. This option suggests only 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is also correct because de-icing works by glycol inserting into and breaking up the regular hydrogen-bonded lattice of ice, lowering the melting point.
options.D: Incorrect. This option suggests only 1 is correct. Statements 2 and 3 are also correct. Students choosing this may forget that alcohols hydrogen bond to themselves and that like dissolves like for -OH compounds in water.
